references.text: Moses expresses similar doubts about his authority and credibility before the people of Israel.
God assures Moses that the elders of the people will listen to his voice, in contrast to Moses' fear.
The people finally believed when they heard that the Lord had looked upon them, in response to Moses' concern.
The Israelites did not listen to Moses because of discouragement, confirming Moses' fear.
The people's unbelief and questions about the Lord's presence reflect Moses' worry that they would not believe.
The question of who believed the message is linked to the theme of unbelief toward God's messengers.
John quotes Isaiah regarding the people's unbelief despite signs, paralleling Moses' fear that the people would not believe.
Moses' fear in Ex 4:1 that the people would not listen to him is confirmed as an actual observation later in the narrative (Ex 6:12).
Moses' fear in Ex 4:1 that Pharaoh would not listen is fulfilled and explained theologically as God's plan in Ex 11:9.
Moses' fear that the people would not listen (Ex 4:1) is mirrored in God's historical observation of Israel's enduring resistance to prophets (Jer 29:19).
A theological parallel between Moses' fear of unbelief (Ex 4:1) and Jesus' confrontation with the same resistance (Lk 22:67).
Jeremiah 15:1 uses Moses as an example that even his efforts would not help if the people did not listen, highlighting the seriousness of the fear in Ex 4:1.
